                    ### Question
                    A 34-year-old woman with a history of depression is brought to the emergency department by her husband 45 minutes after ingesting an unknown amount of a termite poison in a suicide attempt. She has abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. Her husband reports that she has had two episodes of watery diarrhea on the way to the emergency department. A distinct, garlic-like odor on the breath is noted on examination. An ECG shows sinus tachycardia and QTc prolongation. Administration of which of the following is most appropriate?

                    ### Options
                    opa. N-acetylcysteine
opb. Fomepizole
opc. Deferoxamine
opd. Physostigmine
ope. Dimercaprol

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
In this case of suspected organophosphate poisoning presenting with gastrointestinal symptoms, watery diarrhea, garlic-like odor on breath, and QTc prolongation on ECG, the most appropriate administration is Fomepizole, not Physostigmine. Physostigmine is contraindicated in organophosphate poisoning due to the risk of exacerbating cholinergic crisis. Fomepizole is the preferred antidote for toxic alcohol poisoning, including methanol and ethylene glycol, which can present similarly to organophosphate poisoning.
